item.title: PandaFS: Distributed File System in Go
item.description: Creating a robust and efficient file system is a significant challenge when you want it to survive the apocalypse. This blog chronicles the development of a distributed file system in Go, which I (not so) lovingly call PandaFS.

item.title: About
item.description:
Hi, I’m Abhinav an engineer, tinkerer and lifelong learner. Welcome to my little (and as of now, somewhat barren) scratchpad on the internet.

I’m currently studying Computer Science and Engineering at PES University.
I’ve worked as an Software Engineering Intern at Arista Networks in the summer of 2024, and as a open-source contributor in Google Summer of Code in the summer of 2023.

I’m interested in Game Development, Computer Graphics, and low level systems in general. I build to understand, and to make my life easier. You can check out my blogs or my Github to see some of the projects I have built.

item.title: Projects
item.description:
PandaFS
Distributed File System written in Go with built-in replication and fault tolerance for datanodes. Supports a tree based hierarchy with standard metadata operations.

Tungsten (WIP)
Centralised Version Control System à la Subversion and Perforce. Built to version video game projects. Written in Rust.

NCFE-EVM
Computer voting program using Python, Flask, HTML/CSS, and MongoDB. Deployed in the real world to service over 1000+ voters.

quickhash
Rust application to find and the verify checksum(s) of a file or directory of files.
